headline: GPT-Live-1 now available in the API for real-time applications
summary: OpenAI has integrated its new GPT-Live-1 model into its API, allowing developers to access its capabilities for real-time applications and interactive AI experiences.
details: OpenAI has officially rolled out GPT-Live-1, its latest generative AI model, making it accessible to developers via its API. This integration is expected to enable new real-time applications and interactive AI experiences.

The 'Live' designation suggests enhanced capabilities for processing and responding to information in real-time, potentially improving conversational AI, live content generation, and dynamic data analysis.

Developers can now leverage GPT-Live-1 to build more responsive and interactive AI-powered features into their applications, from advanced chatbots to dynamic content platforms. This expands the potential for AI integration across various industries.

Further details on specific performance benchmarks and pricing for GPT-Live-1 are anticipated. OpenAI typically provides extensive documentation and examples to help developers quickly adopt new models.

headline_marked: [[California signs landmark laws]] restricting youth social media and AI chatbot use
headline: California signs landmark laws restricting youth social media and AI chatbot use
summary: The new legislation restricts social media's 'addictive features' for users under 16 and mandates safety protocols, including mental health resources, for AI chatbots interacting with minors.
details: California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed multiple measures aimed at protecting the state's youth. These new laws include restrictions for potentially addictive social media features and limitations on how young users can interact with AI chatbots.

Chatbot makers will be required to implement mental health resources, safety protocols in case a minor discusses self harm and notifications for parents if a child turns off safety settings. California will now require 'independent child safety audits and annual risk assessments' by AI companies, with legal liability for non-compliance.

One of the more divisive measures prohibits social media companies from letting users under age 16 access potentially 'addictive features.' This definition includes wide-ranging capabilities from autoplaying videos to notifications and personalized algorithm-driven content feeds.

Critics like the Electronic Frontier Foundation called this measure a functional ban on social media for teens. They argue it could force all social media users to disclose more personal information to prove their age, creating additional privacy risks.

Additional measures signed include an expanded definition of child sexual exploitation to include generative AI-made or digitally altered images. Another bill offers new protections against targeted advertising and regulates AI systems' use of data about K-12 students.
